eligibility: Step 0 requires histologic or cytologic prostate cancer, including neuroendocrine, small-cell, and sarcomatoid variants, without central pathology review and without using histology to select the arm.

Measurable or non-measurable metastatic disease by RECIST 1.1 is required, and tissue from any time during mCRPC or within 12 months before pre-registration must be available, with metastasis preferred and no mandated repeat biopsy for a later pre-registration.

A CLIA next-generation sequencing report is required, the molecular tumor board assigns the arm, qualifying DNA may come from tumor at any time or ctDNA within 12 months, and RNA assignment requires Caris testing of tumor from the mCRPC period or within 12 months when no qualifying DNA alteration is found.
Age is 18 or older.
Step 1 requires progressive mCRPC with testosterone below 50 ng/dL plus PSA progression, RECIST 1.1 soft-tissue progression, or PCWG3 bone progression.

PSA progression is two consecutive rises at least 1 week apart, the most recent PSA at least 2.0 ng/mL when PSA is the only sign of progression, and antiandrogen withdrawal before counting PSA progression if an antiandrogen was used.

Patients assigned to lutetium must have investigator-assessed PSMA-positive mCRPC; the protocol cites the VISION reference of at least one lesion with uptake above liver and no PSMA-negative node of short axis at least 2.5 cm, solid-organ lesion of short axis at least 1.0 cm, or bone lesion with a soft-tissue component of short axis at least 1.0 cm.

A prior androgen-receptor signaling inhibitor in metastatic hormone-sensitive disease or mCRPC is required, a prior taxane in either setting is required unless the patient is taxane-ineligible or refuses, prior lutetium is allowed, and deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1 or BRCA2 requires a prior PARP inhibitor.
Prior toxicity must be grade 1 or less or at baseline, except alopecia, and stable grade 2 neuropathy, fatigue, and the listed endocrinopathies are allowed.

No cytotoxic, biologic, radiopharmaceutical, or other non-kinase investigational agent is allowed within 4 weeks, kinase inhibitors and abiraterone, apalutamide, or darolutamide must stop at least 2 weeks before registration, enzalutamide must stop at least 4 weeks before, radiotherapy must stop at least 2 weeks before, major surgery must stop at least 4 weeks before, and prior EZH-inhibitor treatment is excluded.
The registration checklist also prints a separate bullet, 'Prior treatment with cabazitaxel + carboplatin,' and does not say whether that treatment is required, allowed, or excluded.

Current moderate or strong CYP3A inducers and hypersensitivity to valemetostat tosylate (DS-3201b) are exclusions; HIV with an undetectable viral load on antiretroviral therapy within 6 months is allowed; hepatitis B must be undetectable on suppression if indicated; and hepatitis C must be cured or undetectable on treatment.

Imminent or established spinal cord compression is excluded, and brain metastases or cranial epidural disease must be treated and stable for at least 4 weeks after radiotherapy or surgery, with wound healing complete.

Myocardial infarction or uncontrolled angina within 6 months, NYHA class 3 or 4 heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension above 160 mmHg systolic or 100 mmHg diastolic, QTcF of 470 ms or higher within 42 days in a patient with cardiac history or a QT-prolonging medication, a clinically significant acute infection requiring systemic therapy, and Child-Pugh class B or C liver disease are exclusions.
ECOG performance status is 0-2, sperm cannot be frozen or donated within 14 days, and G-CSF, red-cell transfusion, platelet transfusion within 2 weeks, and a bleeding diathesis are exclusions.

Labs are WBC at least 2,500/mcL, ANC above 1,500/mcL, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, platelets at least 100,000/mcL, Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (at most 3 x ULN in Gilbert disease), AST and ALT at most 3 x ULN, and albumin at least 2.8 g/dL, and registration waits for the tumor-board assignment.

One re-registration is allowed after progression on the assigned therapy, without reconsent, and requires testosterone below 50 ng/dL, radiographic progression on CT or MRI of chest, abdomen, and pelvis plus a bone scan within 42 days, the same performance status, transfusion, cardiac, and laboratory limits, with transfusions allowed for the hemoglobin threshold and QTcF below 470 ms when cardiac history or a QT-affecting condition is present, plus a new Caris-based tumor-board assignment.
